title: Hamzated Verbs II — Middle & Final Hamza
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 26; Ryding Ch. 2 §2.3.2, Ch. 22 §22.4)
objectives: Conjugate verbs with hamza as middle radical (سَأَلَ) or final radical (قَرَأَ).
Apply the vowel-strength hierarchy (kasrah > ḍammah > fatḥah > sukūn) to choose the hamza seat (kursī).
Spell medial and final hamza forms accurately across tenses and moods.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 25: Why does 1s imperfect of أَخَذَ write آخُذُ with maddah?

sections.heading: Choosing the Seat of Hamza (Kursī al-Hamzah)
sections.body: Medial and final hamzated verbs conjugate completely regularly in sound—only the written seat (kursī) of the hamza changes depending on the surrounding vowels: yāʾ without dots (ئـ), wāw (ؤ), alif (أ), or on the line (ء).

sections.label: Vowel-Strength Hierarchy
sections.summary: Compare the vowel ON the hamza and the vowel BEFORE it; the stronger vowel determines the seat: Kasrah (ـِ → ئـ) > Ḍammah (ـُ → ؤ) > Fatḥah (ـَ → أ) > Sukūn (ـْ). At the end of a word, only the vowel BEFORE the hamza determines the seat.

sections.heading: Hamza Seat Examples
rows: Final hamza preceded by fatḥah → أ
Fatḥah before ḍammah → ؤ (or أ before و)

sections.translation: The scholar was asked about the issue.
sections.irab: سُئِلَ: فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ مَبْنِيٌّ لِلْمَجْهُولِ | العَالِمُ: نَائِبُ فَاعِلٍ مَرْفُوعٌ
sections.notes: In سُئِلَ, the hamza carries kasrah after ḍammah; since kasrah is the strongest vowel, it sits on ئـ.

sections.heading: Final Hamza After Sukūn or Long Vowel
sections.body: When a final hamza is preceded by sukūn or a long vowel (e.g., شَيْءٌ, جَاءَ, مَقْرُوءٌ), it sits on the line (ء).
